title: Why Smells Make Us Feel At Home

blanks.sentence: For the brain, one of the strongest signs of home is _____.
One presenter associated home with pine, damp and _____.
Another remembered a parent’s perfume and a father’s _____.
After a long trip, a house may smell a bit _____.
One possible reason is that the house has been _____ for weeks.
The normal smell of home often remains _____ while people are living there.
Receptor cells in the nose detect air _____.
Olfactory organs analyse smells for possible _____.
We stop noticing the smell of home because it is not a _____.
Even unnoticed, home scent is linked with comfort and _____.

multipleChoice.question: What central claim is made about home and the brain?
options: Visual details are the only way to recognise home
Smell can strongly identify a place as home
People recognise home mainly through sound
The brain ignores smell completely

multipleChoice.question: Why are pine, damp, books, perfume and soap mentioned?
options: To list dangerous household chemicals
To compare expensive and cheap smells
To show everyone dislikes home smells
To give examples of smells connected with home

multipleChoice.question: When might people especially notice their home’s smell?
options: After returning from a long trip
Only when moving to a new country
Before leaving for work each day
While watching television at home

multipleChoice.question: What alternative explanation is given for a strange smell at home?
options: The home must have become unsafe
The smell is always caused by cooking
It may simply be the usual smell that was previously unnoticed
The smell proves the house has no ventilation

multipleChoice.question: What happens when we breathe in, according to the explanation?
options: The brain immediately removes all emotions
Nose receptor cells detect molecules in the air
The house stops producing any smell
The limbic system blocks every signal

multipleChoice.question: What function do olfactory organs perform?
options: They analyse smells for danger
They create molecules in the nose
They make familiar smells stronger
They prevent people from breathing smoke

multipleChoice.question: Why does filtering out familiar smells help us?
options: It makes all ordinary smells disappear forever
It stops people from remembering their homes
It makes pleasant smells become dangerous
It helps us notice unusual smells that may signal danger

multipleChoice.question: What is the burning toast example used to show?
options: People usually prefer burnt food
Smoke is never treated as a threat
A change in smell can alert the brain to possible harm
The scent of home always smells like toast

multipleChoice.question: What does the word “entangled” suggest about scent and home?
options: Home scent is closely connected with feelings of comfort and safety
Home scent is separate from emotional memory
Only dangerous smells affect the brain
People can never recognise comfort through smell

multipleChoice.question: What broader conclusion is given about smell?
options: Smell affects only the nose, not the brain
Home smells matter only when they are unpleasant
Smell is weaker than all other senses
Smell is strongly linked to memory, emotion and feeling at home
